questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains grammatical error(s).

At the zoo, a curious child / fed an elephant some peanuts, / while enthusiastic group of the visitors / watched in amazement.

options.text: At the zoo, a curious child
while enthusiastic group of the visitors

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase "**while enthusiastic group of the visitors**" is grammatically incorrect due to a missing article.
 
• Before a singular countable noun like "**group**", an article is required — here, it should be "**an enthusiastic group**".
 
• Also, the phrase "**of the visitors**" is correct, but the article must come before the adjective "enthusiastic" that qualifies "group".
 
• So, the corrected phrase should be: "**while an enthusiastic group of the visitors**".

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"At the zoo, a curious child fed an elephant some peanuts, while **an enthusiastic group of the visitors** watched in amazement."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** Grammatically correct – it sets the scene.
 
• **Option 3:** Correct usage of verb and object – "fed an elephant some peanuts."
 
• **Option 4:** Correct past tense and adverb phrase – "watched in amazement."

questions.question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

This is one of best movies I have ever seen.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase "one of best" is incorrect because the article "the" is required before the adjective "best."
 
• The correct phrase should be "one of **the best** movies I have ever seen."
 
• Thus, the error is located in **part A** of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"This is one of **the best** movies I have ever seen."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **B: "This is"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **C: "I have ever seen"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **D: "movies"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.

questions.question:
**Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'.**

Everyone must participate in this session as it is on a subject that __affects__ the community.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'No improvement required'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is grammatically correct.
 
• Here, all the grammatical rules are being followed.
 
• We know that '**that**' is a **relative** **pronoun**. So, after it, the verb should be used according to its **antecedent**.
 
• We tend to go for option 2 but it would be incorrect because '**effects**' is a **noun**. We need a **verb** here instead.
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 1.**

 

**Correct Sentence:__** *Everyone must participate in this session as it is on a subject that **affects** the community.*

questions.question:
Change the following sentence into positive degree.

Sushma is one of the smartest girls in the class.

options.text: Few girls in the class are as smart as Sushma.
Sushma is the smart girl of the class.
Sushma is smarter than any other girls in the class.
No other girl is as smart as Sushma.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. Few girls in the class are as smart as Sushma.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence uses a **superlative degree**, "Sushma is one of the smartest girls in the class."
 
• To change the sentence into **positive degree**, we need to express the comparison in a way that compares Sushma's intelligence to the other girls without using superlative or comparative forms like "smartest" or "smarter."
 
• Option 1, "Few girls in the class are as smart as Sushma," correctly expresses the idea in the **positive degree**.
 
• Other options either use incorrect grammar or fail to convert the sentence into **positive degree**.

Correct Sentence: *Few girls in the class are as smart as Sushma*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Degrees of Comparison:**

 
 
• **Positive Degree:** Describes a quality without making comparisons.

 **Example:** Few girls are as smart as Sushma.
 
• **Comparative Degree:** Compares two entities.

 **Example:** Sushma is smarter than any other girl in the class.
 
• **Superlative Degree:** Highlights the highest degree of quality among three or more entities.

 **Example:** Sushma is one of the smartest girls in the class.

questions.question: Which of the following sentences contains an error in the use of a phrasal verb?

options.text: Let's call off the picnic as there is a possibility of heavy rain.
Can you please take care for my belongings for some time?
It is wise to put up with one's quarrelsome neighbours.
While visiting the library, I came across an interesting book.

questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**To answer this question, let's break down each sentence to identify the error in the use of a phrasal verb:**

__
 
• **1) Let's call off the picnic as there is a possibility of heavy rain.**

 
 
• This sentence correctly uses the phrasal verb "call off" meaning to cancel.
 
• This sentence is grammatically and contextually correct__.
 
 
 
• **2) Can you please take care for my belongings for some time?**
 __
 
• This sentence incorrectly uses the phrasal verb "take care for".
 
• The correct phrase is "take care of".
 
• The sentence is erroneous__ because "for" should be replaced with "of".
 
• **The correct sentence would be:** "Can you please take care of my belongings for some time?"
 
 
 
• **3) It is wise to put up with one's quarrelsome neighbours.**
 __
 
• This sentence correctly uses the phrasal verb "put up with" meaning to tolerate.
 
• This sentence is grammatically and contextually correct__.
 
 
 
• **4) While visiting the library, I came across an interesting book.**
 __
 
• This sentence correctly uses the phrasal verb "come across" meaning to find by chance.
 
• This sentence is grammatically and contextually correct__.
 
 
 
• __So, out of the given sentences, only sentence 2 is erroneous due to incorrect use of the phrasal verb__.
 
• **Therefore, the correct answer is "Option 2."**
